places.w: Opened in 2001 as the first Universal Studios park in Asia; one of Japan's most visited theme parks, with areas including The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and Super Nintendo World.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Super Nintendo World (the world's first, 2021) — Mario Kart, Donkey Kong Country and Nintendo characters, plus Harry Potter, Minions and seasonal anime collabs · theme park

places.ad: 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka (Tempozan Harbor Village), Japan
places.w: One of Japan's largest aquariums, built around a 5,400-ton central Pacific tank holding a whale shark, with exhibits themed on the Pacific Rim.

places.ad: Tempozan Harbor Village, 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: A 112.5 m Ferris wheel beside Kaiyūkan in Tempozan Harbor Village, with a roughly 15-minute ride over Osaka Bay and the city skyline.

places.ad: Osaka Prefectural Government Sakishima Building, 1-14-16 Nanko-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Observation deck 252 m up atop the Sakishima building (completed 1995), giving a 360-degree panorama of Osaka Bay; known for night views.
Head shrine of over two thousand Sumiyoshi shrines across Japan, protecting travellers and sailors; its four main halls face west in the ancient Sumiyoshi-zukuri style.

places.n: Mozu Kofun Group — Daisen Kofun (Emperor Nintoku's Tomb)
places.w: Cluster of 5th-century keyhole tombs in Sakai, UNESCO World Heritage (2019) with the Furuichi group; Daisen Kofun, attributed to Emperor Nintoku, is the largest grave in the world by area (~840 m with moats). The mound itself is off-limits.

places.ad: Daisen Park, 2 Mozu Yugumo-cho, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Museum in Daisen Park tracing the history of the port town of Sakai, starting with the kofun tombs and artifacts excavated from them.

places.n: Expo '70 Commemorative Park & Tower of the Sun
places.w: Vast park on the grounds of the 1970 Japan World Exposition, the first in Asia; Tarō Okamoto's 70 m Tower of the Sun stands over the main entrance as its icon.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Crayon Shin-chan: The Adult Empire Strikes Back (2001) and 20th Century Boys (the real tower dressed as the 'Tomodachi tower', 2009) — ja.wikipedia 太陽の塔 · park / monument

places.w: Forested valley just north of Osaka with a roughly 3 km riverside trail from Hankyu Minoo Station to the 33 m Minoo Waterfall; famous for autumn colours.
Mountain temple above Minoh known as the temple of victory, its grounds dotted with thousands of small red daruma dolls left by wishers.

places.ad: 10-1 Senri Expo Park, Suita, Osaka, Japan
places.w: One of the world's largest ethnology museums, inside the Expo '70 Commemorative Park, with a huge exhibition of everyday artifacts from cultures around the world.
Hands-on museum in Ikeda, birthplace of instant ramen (Momofuku Ando, 1958); at My Cup Noodles Factory visitors design a cup and pick their own soup and toppings.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Momofuku Ando instant-ramen pop culture — where Chicken Ramen (1958) was invented · museum

places.w: Widely considered Japan's finest surviving feudal castle — the white 'White Heron' keep is a National Treasure and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993).
Hillside district where foreign merchants and diplomats settled after Kobe port opened in the 19th century; dozens of Western-style mansions (ijinkan) survive, many open as museums.
Waterfront park on reclaimed land in Kobe's port, home to the red 108 m Kobe Port Tower (1963), the Kobe Maritime Museum and the Earthquake Memorial.
Shopping and entertainment waterfront between JR Kobe Station and the port, popular at night for its harbour views.

places.ad: Sakaemachi-dori / Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku, Kobe, Hyogo, Japan
places.w: The biggest Chinatown in western Japan, packed with more than 100 shops and restaurants and street-food stalls.
One of Japan's oldest shrines, said to be founded in the 3rd century by Empress Jingū; the name Kobe derives from 'Kanbe', the families who served it.
One of Japan's three most famous hot springs, over Mount Rokko from central Kobe; known for its iron-rich 'kinsen' gold and clear 'ginsen' silver waters, explorable on foot.
Four waterfalls (the tallest, Ontaki, 43 m) a short walk from Shin-Kobe Station; the Nunobiki Ropeway climbs above them to one of Japan's largest herb gardens.
The 931 m high point of the Rokko range behind Kobe, with panoramic views over Kobe and Osaka, especially at sunset and night.
Spanning the Akashi Strait to Awaji Island, it was long the world's longest suspension bridge (central span 1,991 m).
Kōbō Daishi's mausoleum at the end of a cemetery path through ancient cedars lined with over 200,000 graves; part of the UNESCO 'Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range'.
Head temple of Shingon Buddhism on Mount Kōya, founded by Kōbō Daishi in the 9th century; within the Kii Mountains UNESCO site.
Reconstructed castle keep on a hill in central Wakayama with free Nishinomaru garden and the maple-filled Momijidani garden and covered wooden bridge.
Castle-town keep (burned 1827, rebuilt 1954) halfway between Osaka and Wakayama, with 360-degree views over Osaka Bay; the town is famous for the Danjiri float festival.
Bayfront district one stop from Kansai Airport with the 256 m SiS Rinku Tower (Rinku Gate Tower Building), Rinku Premium Outlets (200+ shops) and Aeon Mall.

places.n: Kansai Airport Observation Hall Sky View
places.w: Observation hall at Kansai International Airport with 360-degree runway views, an aviation shop and the Sky Museum.
Japan's oldest operating amusement park ('Hira-Par'), with around 40 attractions including the ~80 m Sky Walker Ferris wheel.
6th-century keyhole mound believed to be the true tomb of Emperor Keitai; unusually open to walk on, with replica haniwa on display and the Imashirozuka Ancient History Museum next door.
Nine walled Edo-style gardens built in 1992 on the site of former samurai residences beside Himeji Castle's west moat.

places.n: Umeda Sky Building — Kuchū Teien Floating Garden Observatory
places.ad: Umeda Sky Building, northwest of JR Osaka Station, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: The 173 m twin-tower skyscraper (1993) joined at the top by the open-air Floating Garden observation deck — 360° views over Osaka, open till 22:30.
Temma's shrine to Sugawara no Michizane, god of learning, at the head of Tenjinbashi-suji; home of the Tenjin Matsuri.
The national mint where Japan's coins are struck; famous for opening its riverside avenue of cherry trees to the public each spring.

places.ad: HEP Five, east of Hankyu Umeda, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: A red Ferris wheel bursting from the roof of the HEP shopping complex in Umeda — 106 m high, with views over Kita.
Hideyoshi's 1583 castle, rebuilt in 1931 — the main keep (a museum with a top-floor lookout) rises from stone walls and moats in a vast park famous for plum and cherry blossom.
The canal-side heart of kuidaore Osaka: neon, mechanised signs (the Glico Running Man, the Kani Doraku crab) and street food that barely closes.
"Osaka's Kitchen": a several-hundred-metre covered arcade of fishmongers, butchers, greengrocers and grill-it-on-the-spot stalls.
Osaka's premier shopping street — a ~600 m covered arcade mixing chain stores, boutiques and department stores, running north from Dōtonbori.
Osaka's answer to Harajuku: thrift stores, cafes and youth fashion around Triangle Park, west of Mido-suji.
The 'New World' district built after the 1903 Expo — half Paris, half Coney Island — around Tsūtenkaku, the 103 m tower rebuilt in 1956; the home of Osaka kushikatsu.
Founded by Prince Shōtoku in 593 — one of Japan's oldest temples and the first built by the state, with its five-storey pagoda on the classic straight-line layout.

places.ad: Tennōji Park, Chausuyamacho, Tennoji-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Osaka's city zoo (1915) in Tennōji Park, below Tsūtenkaku.

places.n: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
places.ad: Tennōji Park, Chausuyamacho, Tennoji-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: The 1936 municipal art museum in Tennōji Park, with Keitakuen garden behind it.
Opened 2001 in a tower beside NHK Osaka, across from the castle: large-scale models chronicle the city from its days as Japan's first capital to the early Shōwa era, with views over the castle park.
Contemporary Japanese and international art on two underground floors of Nakanoshima; the 2007 building's entrance structure is designed to evoke growing bamboo.
Hands-on science museum and planetarium on Nakanoshima, next to the National Museum of Art.
The city art museum that opened on Nakanoshima in February 2022 — modern and contemporary art and design, part of the island's museum cluster.
Claimed as Japan's longest covered shopping street — 2.6 km of shops and eateries running north from the Tenmangū approach.

A moss-covered Fudō Myōō statue that worshippers splash with water, beside two 80 m stone-paved alleys of old kappo counters, bars and okonomiyaki shops — the setting of Oda Sakunosuke's 'Meoto Zenzai'.
Osaka's Akihabara: electronics, anime, games and maid cafés along Sakaisuji in Nipponbashi.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Kansai's otaku district — Nipponbashi Ota Road, Animate, Mandarake and Jungle for anime, manga, figures and retro games · electronics & otaku district

places.w: Osaka's grown-up entertainment quarter just south of Osaka Station — hundreds of restaurants, hostess bars and counters.
A pocket of pre-war row houses east of Umeda whose narrow lanes are now full of cafés, craft shops and vintage stores.
Osaka's oldest tutelary shrine, an Engishiki-listed great shrine to the land deities Ikushima and Tarushima, on the Uemachi ridge near Tanimachi 9-chōme.

places.ad: Osaka Castle Park, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Shrine inside Osaka Castle Park enshrining Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Hideyori and Hidenaga as deities of success — a branch of Kyoto's Toyokuni Shrine.
Jon Jerde's 2003 mall on the old Osaka Stadium site, shaped like a canyon of rock strata, with ~70,000 plants on its terraced rooftop Parks Garden.
Japan's largest Koreatown: about 150 grocers, kimchi and chijimi stalls, restaurants and hanbok shops along a 300 m shopping street in Ikuno, a short walk from Tsuruhashi's yakiniku alleys.
The nation's most prestigious stage for bunraku, Osaka's own puppet theatre — runs of about three weeks in January, April, June, July/August and November.
The Umekita redevelopment beside JR Osaka Station — a large urban park with new towers opening in stages through spring 2027, next to the Grand Front Osaka complex.
Open lawns and reconstructed platform bases across from Osaka Castle Park marking the 7th–8th-century imperial palace of Naniwa-kyō, when Osaka was Japan's capital.
The ~300 m skyscraper that opened in 2014 — department store, hotel, art museum and the Harukas 300 observation deck with panoramic views across Osaka.

places.ad: Tennōji Park, Chausuyamacho, Tennoji-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: A 19,800 m² strolling pond garden behind the city art museum, designed by tea master Kizu Issai and built by Ogawa Jihei VII (of Heian Shrine and Murin-an fame); entry is just ¥150.
The park holding the zoo, greenhouse, art museum and Keitakuen, fronted by 'Tenshiba' — a Good Design Award-winning lawn with cafés a short walk from Tennōji Station.

places.n: Ebisubashi & the Glico Running Man sign
places.ad: Ebisubashi bridge, Dōtonbori, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: The bridge over the Dōtonbori canal where everyone poses with the Glico Running Man — the neon heart of Minami's mechanised signs.

Famous for its 12 m-high lion-head stage, whose gaping mouth swallows bad luck and brings victory in competition; the shrine was rebuilt after the 1945 air raids and keeps an intangible-folk-culture tug-of-war rite.
Yoshimoto's 858-seat 'hall of laughter', Japan's largest comedy theatre — Yoshimoto Shinkigeki, manzai and rakugo 365 days a year.
Shinsekai's 130 m covered alley of kushikatsu and doteyaki counters and old game parlours, running south toward Dōbutsuen-mae.

places.n: LUCUA Characters World — Pokémon Center Osaka & Nintendo OSAKA
places.ad: LUCUA SOUTH 10–13F (South Gate Building), JR Osaka Station, Umeda, Kita-ku, Osaka
places.w: Osaka's answer to Tokyo's Character Street: LUCUA SOUTH opened 5 April 2026 and gathered Pokémon Center Osaka, Nintendo OSAKA and the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store (moved from Daimaru Umeda) on its top floors, growing to 30+ character shops (Sanrio, Square Enix, Minecraft) by autumn 2026.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon · Nintendo (Mario, Zelda, Splatoon) · One Piece — Kansai's biggest official character-store cluster, the Pokémon Center and Nintendo flagship stores of western Japan · character shops, pop culture

places.w: Memorial museum to the 'God of Manga' (Astro Boy, Black Jack, Phoenix) in Takarazuka, the town where he grew up — permanent display of his life and work plus rotating exhibitions, ~30 min by train from Osaka. Note: special long closure 1 Dec 2026 – 4 Mar 2027.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Osamu Tezuka (Astro Boy / Tetsuwan Atom, Black Jack, Princess Knight) — the founding father of modern manga and TV anime, in his hometown · museum

places.ad: Wakamatsu Park, Wakamatsu-chō, Nagata-ku, Kobe, Hyōgo
places.w: A full-scale 18 m steel Tetsujin-28 robot raised in Wakamatsu Park by the KOBE Tetsujin Project as a symbol of recovery from the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake; Nagata was creator Mitsuteru Yokoyama's hometown. Short walk from Shin-Nagata Station.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Tetsujin 28-go (Gigantor) by Mitsuteru Yokoyama — a life-size giant robot honouring the Kobe-born manga pioneer and the earthquake recovery · statue, monument

places.w: Kansai's first Anpanman Children's Museum (2013) at Kobe Harborland: hands-on play museum with daily stage shows and an Anpanman bakery and shop in a free-entry mall — the go-to stop for families with small children.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Soreike! Anpanman (Takashi Yanase) — Japan's best-loved preschool anime hero, with his own bakery-themed museum · museum, family

places.ad: Near JR Ōtori Station, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Ichinomiya (first shrine) of old Izumi Province, c. 1,900 years old, enshrining Yamato Takeru; a five-minute walk from JR Ōtori Station.
Ancient Kōyasan Shingon temple (founded 701, restored by Kūkai 815) holding the National Treasure Nyoirin Kannon and Kondō hall; plum, cherry and autumn-leaf spot.
Mountain temple patronised by Toyotomi Hideyoshi (his letter survives here), with National Treasure Buddhist statues shown in autumn special exhibitions.

places.n: Chikatsu Asuka Museum (大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館)
places.w: Tadao Ando's stepped kofun-shaped museum of Japan's burial-mound age, set in the Chikatsu Asuka Fudoki-no-Oka tomb park.
places.nat: 大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館

places.ad: In front of Hamadera Ekimae / Hamadera-kōen Station, Sakai & Takaishi, Osaka, Japan
places.w: One of the prefecture's oldest parks (1873), a seaside pine grove at the end of the Hankai tram; the Tatsuno Kingo-office Hamadera-kōen station building is a rare Meiji survivor.
Museum of the Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri — the September festival where carved wooden floats are hauled at a run round street corners.
Hundertwasser-designed waste plant on an artificial island — red, black and white walls, a golden onion tower and roof greenery; free guided interior tours by reservation.

places.ad: Tempozan Park, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: 'Japan's lowest mountain' — a 4.5 m summit marker inside a harbourside park with a hidden cherry-blossom grove and an Emperor Meiji monument; 7 min from Osakakō Station.

places.ad: Tempozan Harbor Village, 1 Kaigan-dōri, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: The harbour mall at the heart of Tempozan Harbor Village, beside the Ferris wheel and Kaiyūkan; inside are the retro Shōwa food alley Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokochō and LEGOLAND Discovery Center Osaka.
Kawachi's ichinomiya at the foot of the Ikoma range, said to date back 2,600+ years; famous for its plum grove and the 23 December 'laughing ritual' (Owarai Shinji).

places.n: Ishikiri Tsurugiya Shrine (石切劔箭神社)
places.w: 'Ishikiri-san', the god of swellings — nationally known for the ohyakudo-mairi, worshippers circling between the stones and the hall, and a fortune-teller-lined approach street.
Japan's largest greenhouse botanical garden, built as Osaka's pavilion for Expo '90 in Tsurumi Ryokuchi Park — ~15,000 plants of 5,500 species.
Birthplace of Japanese malt whisky (built 1923): whisky museum, paid tastings and a lottery-entry production tour; 10 min walk from JR Yamazaki / Hankyu Ōyamazaki.

places.n: Open-Air Museum of Old Japanese Farmhouses (日本民家集落博物館)
places.w: Japan's first open-air museum (1956), in Hattori Ryokuchi Park: 11 relocated 17th-19th-century folk houses from Iwate to Amami Ōshima.
En no Gyōja-founded temple on the Minoo Falls trail, home to one of Japan's four great Benzaiten and billed as the birthplace of the Japanese lottery; 15 min walk from Hankyu Minoh.
Shrine to Ame-no-Iwafune, a 12 m boat-shaped boulder up the Amanogawa valley; the 'iwa-kuguri' rock-cave crawl beneath the giant stones is open to visitors.

places.n: Hirakatashuku Kagiya Museum (枚方宿鍵屋資料館)
places.w: Edo-period riverside inn where travellers waited for the Fushimi-Osaka riverboats on the Kyō-kaidō post town; a cultural property, opened as a museum in 2001.

places.n: Engyō-ji (Mount Shosha, 書写山圓教寺)
places.w: Atmospheric 1,000-year-old mountain temple complex 30 min from Himeji by bus and ropeway; the Mitsunodō halls were a set for The Last Samurai.
places.nat: Mount Shosha, 書写山圓教寺

places.n: Furuichi Kofun Group — Konda Gobyōyama Kofun (誉田御廟山古墳)
places.w: The second-largest keyhole tomb in Japan (attributed to Emperor Ōjin), heart of the Furuichi half of the UNESCO Mozu-Furuichi kofun group, next to Konda Hachimangū near Kintetsu Furuichi Station.

places.ad: Kongō range, Chihaya-Akasaka village, Osaka / Nara border, Japan
places.w: Osaka's highest peak (1,125 m) and the prefecture's favourite hike — ropeway, summit shrine and frosted-tree winter scenery in the Kongō-Ikoma-Kisen Quasi-National Park.

places.ad: Senri Banpaku Kōen, Suita, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Entertainment complex beside Expo '70 Park: the Kaiyūkan team's 'living museum' NIFREL and Japan's tallest Ferris wheel, plus a large mall.

places.n: Hoshida Park — Hoshi no Buranko suspension bridge (星のブランコ)
places.ad: Osaka Prefectural Forest Hoshida Park, Katano, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Japan's largest wooden pedestrian suspension bridge, the 'Star Swing', strung across a valley of the Tanabata-legend Amanogawa forest above Katano.

places.n: Hanazono Rugby Stadium (東大阪市花園ラグビー場)
places.w: Japan's oldest rugby-only stadium (1929), the 'holy ground' of the national high-school tournament and a 2019 Rugby World Cup venue; free Hanazono Rugby Museum on match days.
places.nat: 東大阪市花園ラグビー場

places.n: Fujita Museum of Art (藤田美術館)
places.w: Meiji magnate Fujita Denzaburō's collection of ~2,000 Asian artworks — 9 National Treasures (incl. a yōhen tenmoku tea bowl) and 53 Important Cultural Properties — in a rebuilt gallery by Kyōbashi.

places.n: Shiba Ryōtarō Memorial Museum (司馬遼太郎記念館)
places.w: The historical novelist's house and study beside a Tadao Ando library hall whose 11 m wall of shelves holds part of his 60,000-book collection.

places.n: Panasonic Museum (Kōnosuke Matsushita History Museum, Kadoma)
places.w: Free museum at Panasonic's Kadoma home: founder Matsushita Kōnosuke's story, the 'Monozukuri-ism' hall of landmark home appliances, and Sakura Square.

places.n: Kyocera Dome Osaka (京セラドーム大阪)
places.w: Kansai's largest indoor stadium (36,220 seats for baseball), home of the Orix Buffaloes and Osaka's big-concert dome; Tugboat Taishō waterfront food-and-art strip is a short walk away.

places.ad: Chikkō Red Brick Warehouse, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
places.w: Classic-car museum of about 80 landmark cars (e.g. a 1900-1950 Rolls-Royce Phantom II era line-up) inside the 1923 Chikkō red-brick port warehouse near Tempozan.

places.n: Ikeda Castle Ruins Park (池田城跡公園)
places.w: Park (2000) on the site of the Ikeda clan's castle: stroll garden with a central pond, tea room and a lookout tower with views to Takarazuka, Osaka and Kobe.

places.n: Satsukiyama Park & Zoo (五月山公園・五月山動物園)
places.w: Ikeda's hillside park for spring cherry blossom and autumn leaves; at its foot the free Satsukiyama Zoo, Japan's second-smallest, famous for its wombats.
places.nat: 五月山公園・五月山動物園

places.n: Itsuō Art Museum & Kobayashi Ichizō Memorial Hall (逸翁美術館)
places.w: Collection of Hankyu/Takarazuka founder Kobayashi Ichizō (pen-name Itsuō) — early-modern paintings and tea ceramics — beside his Gazoku Sansō residence, now the memorial hall.

places.n: Kobe Earthquake Memorial Museum (人と防災未来センター)
places.ad: HAT Kobe, Chūō-ku, Kobe, Hyōgo, Japan
places.w: Memorial museum of the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake (opened 2002): a large-screen recreation of the quake, a recovery documentary and hands-on disaster-prevention exhibits.
places.nat: 人と防災未来センター

places.w: Early-20th-century landscape garden of former Kobe mayor Kodera Kenkichi, public since 1941, with a relocated Western-style residence and boathouse; 300 yen, closed Thursdays.

places.n: Kobe City Museum (神戸市立博物館)
places.ad: Old Settlement (Kyūkyoryūchi), Chūō-ku, Kobe, Hyōgo, Japan
places.w: Archaeology and one of the world's largest collections of Namban art — Japanese painting from the first contact with Western ships in the 1500s — in a former bank in the old foreign settlement.

places.n: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living (大阪くらしの今昔館)
places.w: Walk-through, life-size reconstruction of an Edo-period Osaka merchant townscape on the upper floors of a building at the north end of Tenjinbashi-suji. Closed for renovation until 5 January 2027 (japan-guide e4024) — check before visiting.

places.n: Daisen Park Japanese Garden (大仙公園日本庭園)
places.ad: Daisen Park, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
places.w: 26,000 m² stroll garden of hill, forest and spring evoking medieval Sakai, inside Daisen Park beside Emperor Nintoku's tomb; matcha at the Shinan teahouse; 5 min from JR Mozu.

places.n: Temma Tenjin Hanjo Tei (天満天神繁昌亭, rakugo theatre)
places.w: Osaka's dedicated rakugo hall (yose) beside Osaka Tenmangū — the home stage of Kamigata comic storytelling, with daily shows.
places.nat: 天満天神繁昌亭, rakugo theatre

places.ad: Universal Studios Japan, 2-1-33 Sakurajima, Konohana-ku, Osaka
places.w: The world's first Super Nintendo World opened inside USJ on 18 March 2021 (Mario Kart: Koopa's Challenge, Yoshi's Adventure); the Donkey Kong Country expansion (Mine Cart Madness) opened 11 Dec 2024 and grew the land by ~70%. Timed-entry via the USJ app on busy days.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Nintendo — Super Mario & Donkey Kong; the first Nintendo theme-park land anywhere, built in Osaka · theme-park land

places.ad: Hyōgo Prefectural Awaji Shima Park, Awaji, Hyōgo
places.w: Anime theme park opened 15 July 2017 inside Awaji Shima Park: Naruto & Boruto, Dragon Quest, Crayon Shin-chan, SPY×FAMILY attractions and a life-size Shin Godzilla you zip-line into (Godzilla Interception Operation, 2020). Park entry free; attractions ~¥2,000–6,000. ~90 min by highway bus from Osaka.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Naruto · Godzilla · Dragon Quest · Crayon Shin-chan — Kansai's only multi-franchise anime theme park · anime theme park

places.w: Kitty-head-shaped Sanrio complex on the Seto Inland Sea: an underwater Hello Kitty princess digital-art show plus two restaurants serving on Kitty tableware; the Hello Kitty Show Box (live musical lunch) is a short bus ride away.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Sanrio — Hello Kitty; the Kansai counterpart to Tokyo's Puroland · character attraction

places.w: Home stage of the all-female Takarazuka Revue. Osamu Tezuka grew up nearby and his mother took him here; the Revue's male-role stars, costumes and big sparkling eyes shaped Princess Knight and his whole art style. Pair with the Tezuka Manga Museum a short walk away.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Osamu Tezuka — Princess Knight (Ribbon no Kishi) was directly inspired by the Takarazuka Revue · theatre

places.w: Neo-Renaissance red-brick hall completed 1918 with a donation from stockbroker Einosuke Iwamoto (design Tatsuno Kingo & Okada Shin'ichirō); restored 1999–2002 and designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002. Free basement history exhibit.

1,300-year-old Umeda shrine named for Sugawara no Michizane's dew-and-tears poem; nicknamed after Ohatsu, heroine of Chikamatsu's 1703 'Love Suicides at Sonezaki', set in its grove — now a matchmaking power spot.

Temple founded by Gyōki in 744; its wooden main hall (rebuilt 1808) miraculously survived the WWII air raids amid the Minami neon. Appears in Chikamatsu's Sonezaki Shinjū and the rakugo story 'Mameda'.

CLOSED: Dōtonbori's neo-Renaissance theatre (opened 1923 as a cinema, kabuki/stage house since 1997) gave its final performance, the 'Onagori Gogatsu Ōkabuki', on 26 May 2026 after 103 years; Shochiku plans to demolish the ageing building. Facade-only now — no shows.

pv.ss: Kumamoto Nichinichi (Kyodo) — final performance 26 May 2026, 103 years https://kumanichi.com/articles/1995142 ; ja.wikipedia

places.ad: Namba 1-chōme (corner lot west of Hōzen-ji), Chūō-ku, Osaka
places.w: The only museum anywhere with a permanent display of Kamigata (Osaka-Kyoto) ukiyo-e — realistic kabuki-actor prints of stars like Nakamura Utaemon III, ~30 works over four small floors, plus print-making classes (reservation). Free with the Osaka Amazing Pass.
Jōdo temple where Tokugawa Ieyasu headquartered during the Sieges of Osaka; famous for its okotsu-butsu Buddhas moulded from the ashes of the dead and accepting remains regardless of sect.

places.n: Abe no Seimei Shrine (安倍晴明神社)
places.w: Shrine on the reputed birthplace of the Heian onmyōji Abe no Seimei, with his statue and 'birth-bath' well; an outlying shrine of Abe Ōji Jinja.
Osaka's 'Ebessan', packed by about a million merchants each 9–11 January for Tōka Ebisu lucky-bamboo; first stop on the Osaka Seven Lucky Gods pilgrimage.

places.n: Sakai Traditional Crafts Museum (Sakai Densho-kan) — Sakai knives
places.w: Showcase and shop for Sakai's 600-year knife-forging tradition (plus incense, tea and textiles), with live sharpening demos — Sakai is one of Japan's three great cutlery towns.

places.n: Nisanzai Kofun (土師ニサンザイ古墳)
places.w: One of the largest keyhole tombs of the UNESCO Mozu-Furuichi group (late 5th c.), its moat-ringed mound a quieter, more photogenic alternative to Nintoku's tomb.
Early-Meiji public park and pine grove on the old western approach to Sumiyoshi Taisha, beside Nankai Sumiyoshi-kōen Station.

places.n: Osaka Nanko Bird Sanctuary (大阪南港野鳥園)
places.ad: Nankō-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka (NW corner of Sakishima)
places.w: Free tidal-flat wetland built on Sakishima as a stop-over for migratory shorebirds, with an observation building and tower; closed Wednesdays.

places.ad: Nankō-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka (Sakishima, by Trade Center-mae Stn)
places.w: Big waterfront mall/trade complex on Sakishima beside the Cosmo Tower, with harbour-view boardwalks and the Osaka Bay sunset.
Indoor LEGO attraction (opened 2015) at Tempozan with a Miniland recreating Osaka in bricks, 4D cinema and DUPLO area — for ages 3–10; adults need a child except on adult nights.

26 m mound in Tennōji Park long held to be a 5th-century kofun; it was Tokugawa Ieyasu's HQ in the Winter Siege and Sanada Yukimura's in the Summer Siege of Osaka (1614–15). Summit markers explain the battle.
Small hillside shrine on the Tennōji slopes where Sanada Yukimura is said to have fallen in 1615; also linked to Sugawara no Michizane.

places.n: Sankō Shrine & Sanada Yukimura statue (三光神社)
places.w: Tamatsukuri shrine guarding a bronze statue of Sanada Yukimura and the 'Sanada tunnel' entrance near the site of his Sanada-maru fort.

Neighbourhood sentō near Dōbutsuen-mae with a ceiling painting of 108 carp, soft water throughout and a 110°C Mt Fuji lava-stone sauna; open from 6am (closed Mon). Featured by Time Out Osaka and All About.
Six floors of manga, anime, retro games, idol merch, cosplay and collectibles, vintage to new; Mandarake's Osaka flagship relocated from Amerikamura to Den Den Town in December 2020.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Mandarake — Osaka's flagship used-otaku megastore, the anchor of Den Den Town · shop

places.w: One of western Japan's largest official anime/manga goods stores, the Ota Road anchor; the same building holds Lashinbang, Melonbooks and card-game floors.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Animate — the official anime-goods chain's big Osaka store on Ota Road · shop

places.w: 1956 Sennichimae leisure building whose 2nd-floor warren of tiny bars and the Misono Universe hall made it an Ura-Namba nightlife legend; tenants left at the end of 2024 and the whole building closed on 5 July 2025 ahead of redevelopment.

pv.ss: Time Out Osaka JP: whole building closed 5 Jul 2025 https://www.timeout.jp/osaka/ja/news/last-day-of-misono-universe-072225

places.n: Daimaru Shinsaibashi Main Building (大丸心斎橋店 本館, Vories)
places.w: William Merrell Vories' 1933 neo-Gothic department store on Midōsuji; rebuilt 2019 reusing the original tiled façade, peacock relief and Art Deco interiors — Lmaga runs Vories architecture walks here and OSAKA-INFO lists it as a historic-architecture highlight.
places.nat: 大丸心斎橋店 本館, Vories

places.w: Temple of Aizen Myōō, the deity of love and marriage, whose 1597 Hideyoshi-rebuilt tahōtō pagoda is an Important Cultural Property and the oldest wooden building in Osaka city; its Aizen Matsuri (30 Jun–2 Jul) opens Osaka's summer festival season.

places.n: Abe Ōji Shrine (阿倍王子神社)
places.w: The only surviving Kumano Kodō 'ōji' waypoint shrine inside Osaka city, counted fourth of the 99 Kumano ōji and traditionally founded under Emperor Nintoku.
Meiji-era shrine to the loyalist Kitabatake Akiie and his father Chikafusa, near the site where Akiie fell in 1338; a quiet stop on the Abeno–Sumiyoshi tram walk.

places.n: Spa World (スパワールド, Shinsekai)
places.w: Giant Shinsekai bathhouse with themed European and Asian bath floors (17 hot-spring styles from 12 countries) plus a rooftop pool — Osaka's classic day-long soak.
Kiddy Land's Kansai flagship (renewed April 2017 with Hankyu Sanbangai): character-specialist corners (Snoopy, Rilakkuma, Miffy and more), nekomart and toy/fancy goods.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Character goods — Kiddy Land, Japan's classic character-toy chain, Kansai flagship · shop

places.w: Weekly Shōnen Jump's official shop (One Piece, Dragon Ball, Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen merch) on Daimaru Shinsaibashi's 9th-floor pop-culture zone beside Pokémon Center Osaka DX.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Weekly Shōnen Jump — the magazine's official store (One Piece, Dragon Ball, JJK) · shop

places.n: Shinsaibashi PARCO Character Floors (Chiikawa Land · Donguri Republic)
places.w: Shinsaibashi PARCO's 'POP CULTURE SHINSAIBASHI' floors gather character flagships with photo spots — Chiikawa Land (creator Nagano's official shop, 6F), a large Donguri Republic Ghibli store, Kiddy Land and more; directly linked to Shinsaibashi Station.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Chiikawa & Studio Ghibli — Osaka's character-shop floor (Chiikawa Land, Donguri Republic) · shop

places.w: Bandai's capsule-toy hall — about 1,000 gashapon machines, opened Dec 2020 as the chain's first Kansai store and billed as the region's largest; since March 2023 it trades inside Bandai Namco Cross Store Osaka Umeda, beside the HEP FIVE Ferris wheel.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Gashapon — Bandai's capsule-toy department store, ~1,000 machines of anime/character capsules · shop

places.ad: Miyama, Wakayama City, Wakayama (ferry from Kada Port)
places.w: Four uninhabited islands in the Kitan Strait with overgrown Meiji-era fort ruins, 20 min by ferry from Kada; the real-world model for Hitogashima in Wakayama-born Yoshinori Tanaka's Summer Time Rendering, selected for the 2023 Anime Tourism 88 with Wakayama City.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Summer Time Rendering — model for the series' island Hitogashima; Anime Tourism 88 (2023, Wakayama City) · nature

places.n: Kiyomizu-dera, Osaka (清水寺, Tamade no Taki)
places.ad: Tennōji-ku, Osaka (top of Kiyomizu-zaka, one of the Tennōji Seven Slopes)
places.w: Osaka's own Kiyomizu-dera, with a mini 'Kiyomizu stage' looking toward Tsūtenkaku and the Tamade-no-taki waterfall — the only natural waterfall inside Osaka city; listed by Time Out Osaka and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania (Kiyomizu-zaka).

Taishō-era former Tobita yūkaku brothel building, now a working ryōtei; its lavish interiors are a nationally Registered Tangible Cultural Property (2000) and the go-to place in Japan to step into the world of Demon Slayer's Entertainment District arc, since nothing comparable survives in Tokyo's old Yoshiwara.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Demon Slayer (Kimetsu no Yaiba) — Entertainment District (Yūkaku-hen) arc: surviving Taishō pleasure-quarter interiors featured by Mapple as the arc's real-world pilgrimage spot · historic ryōtei / former yūkaku architecture

places.ad: 13F, South Gate Building (LUCUA SOUTH), 3-1-1 Umeda, Kita-ku, Osaka
places.w: Capcom's third store and first Kansai café (opened Nov 2022) — ~900 Monster Hunter / Resident Evil / Street Fighter goods plus a 56-seat rotating collab café; still trading in 2026 (Ōkami 20th-anniversary collab, June 2026) after the building's 13F became LUCUA SOUTH.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Capcom (Monster Hunter, Resident Evil, Street Fighter, Ōkami) — the publisher's only Kansai store-café, Osaka being Capcom's home city · game store & collab café

places.n: Kotobukiya Nipponbashi (コトブキヤ日本橋)
places.w: Green-signed flagship of the plastic-model and figure maker: Ghibli, Nintendo, Square Enix and Marvel/Star Wars goods on 1F, current anime/game figures and modelling tools on 2F; in OSAKA-INFO's Nipponbashi pop-culture guide and OsakaMania's figure-shop series.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Kotobukiya — figure/plastic-model maker's own Osaka store (anime, game and Ghibli character goods) · shop

places.n: Tamatsukuri Inari Shrine (玉造稲荷神社)
places.ad: Tamatsukuri, Chūō-ku, Osaka (5 min walk from JR Morinomiya / Metro Tamatsukuri exit 1)
places.w: An ancient shrine on the Uemachi plateau, said to date from 12 BC and long linked to the guardianship of Osaka Castle. OSAKA-INFO calls it the 'princess shrine' because all its deities are goddesses, and it draws women praying for good matches and health. It is also tied to the magatama (curved bead) craft the Tamatsukuri district is named for.

places.n: Miyuki-mori Tenjingū (御幸森天神宮, Ikuno Koreatown)
places.w: A shrine at the head of Ikuno Koreatown, said to be founded in 406, where Emperor Nintoku rested on falconry outings ('Miyuki no Mori'). It is registered as one of Osaka City's urban landscape resources, and its 1,600th-anniversary festival was held in 2006.
places.nat: 御幸森天神宮, Ikuno Koreatown

places.w: Small shrine at the edge of Tennōji Park, said to have been founded by Prince Shōtoku for his uncle Emperor Sushun while Shitennō-ji was being built; one of Shitennō-ji's seven associated shrines and known as the shrine that grants 'one wish in a lifetime'. Named for the moat once crossed to reach it.

Hilltop shrine to Emperor Nintoku, founded by imperial decree in 866 at the reputed site of the Naniwa Takatsu Palace and moved here when Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle; famous as the setting of classic rakugo stories, with rakugo still performed in the grounds. Rebuilt after WWII air raids (one Edo-period storehouse survived).

places.n: Kōnoike Shinden Kaisho (鴻池新田会所)
places.ad: Kōnoike Motomachi, Higashi-Ōsaka, Osaka (5 min walk from JR Kōnoike-Shinden Station)
places.w: Estate office built in 1707 by the Kōnoike merchant house to run the farmland reclaimed after the Yamato River was rerouted; the main house and four storehouses were designated Important Cultural Properties in 1980, and the grounds keep a stroll garden. Rare surviving Edo-period land-development office.

places.n: Tsurumi Ryokuchi (Expo '90 Commemorative Park, 花博記念公園鶴見緑地)
places.w: 122-hectare park on the site of the 1990 International Garden and Greenery Exposition, home to the giant Sakuya Konohana Kan greenhouse, seasonal flower gardens, BBQ, camping and sports grounds; free entry except some facilities.
places.nat: Expo '90 Commemorative Park, 花博記念公園鶴見緑地

places.w: Saikoku pilgrimage temple beside the Furuichi kofun; its seated Thousand-Armed Kannon (725) actually has 1,041 hands with an eye on each palm, a National Treasure shown to the public on the 18th of each month.
Small Hineno temple whose two-tiered tahōtō pagoda of 1271, roofed in cypress bark, is a National Treasure — one of the finest Kamakura-period pagodas, rarely visited from nearby Kansai Airport.
Hillside temple in Kaizuka whose Kannon-dō, a five-by-five-bay hall built in the late Kamakura period (1275–1332), is a National Treasure.

Wooded Kuzuha shrine said to stand on the site of Emperor Keitai's Kusuba Palace; its main hall of 1402 and the subsidiary Hachiman shrine hall are Important Cultural Properties, and the grove is one of the 'Eight Views of Hirakata'.

places.n: Senbonmatsu Ōhashi — the 'Megane-bashi' loop bridge (千本松大橋)
places.ad: over the Kizu River, linking Taishō-ku and Nishinari-ku, Osaka
places.w: 1,228 m road bridge (1973) built 33 m above the Kizu River so ships can pass; the two-tier spiral approaches gave it the nickname 'Megane-bashi' (spectacles bridge), and the Taishō side is a three-level loop. Osaka City lists it as a landscape resource, best seen together with the free Senbonmatsu ferry below it.

places.ad: mouth of the Shirinashi River, linking Minato-ku and Taishō-ku, Osaka
places.w: 1,573 m S-curved bridge (1995) over the mouth of the Shirinashi River. Its 250 m central span is Japan's largest for a girder bridge. You can walk across it in about 30 minutes, with a 360° harbour panorama that takes in the Chitose and Shin-Kizugawa bridges. Osaka City and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania both feature it.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (new for 2026) Chinese restaurant whose Hong Kong- and Guangzhou-trained chef serves Sichuan-style mouth-watering chicken and dim sum such as steamed dumplings and pork shumai.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2026) counter-style French restaurant run single-handedly by a seasoned chef, carrying forward classical French cuisine with boldness; named after the film Diva.

Michelin Bib Gourmand (new for 2026) retro bistro hung with French pop posters in a nine-tsubo space; standards include oeufs mayonnaise, pâté de campagne and beef cheek stewed in red wine, plus pasta, in generous sharing portions.
Michelin-selected (2026) kappo opened by an izakaya chef as a sister shop: creative omakase with salty, sake-friendly dishes, wrapping up with seasonal takikomi-gohan or curry rice with free refills.
Michelin Guide-listed Japanese restaurant whose chef trained in Hozenji Yokocho and now cooks cuisine of the "here and now", mindful of how knife technique affects the flavour of sashimi.
Michelin Guide-listed Japanese restaurant in an old family home, run by affable owner-chef Koji Kawahara whose menu abounds with ingenuity (distinction not confirmed in search).
One MICHELIN Star (2026): counter-style Chinese cuisine in which owner-chef Akihito Shintani works Osaka and Kansai ingredients and Kansai food culture into Chinese cooking — "kamigatachuka".
Michelin Bib Gourmand ramen shop whose signature soy-sauce ramen rests on a chicken broth of guinea fowl and free-range chicken raised together by a like-minded farmer.
One MICHELIN Star Japanese restaurant in Tamatsukuri, Tennoji-ku.
Two MICHELIN Stars (newly promoted in the 2026 guide, the only new two-star in Osaka): Japanese cuisine in Ueshio.
Michelin Guide-listed unagi (freshwater eel) restaurant in Katamachi, Miyakojima-ku.
Michelin Guide-listed charcoal yakitori grilled by a former Japan bantamweight boxing champion who took up yakitori as his second "ring"; the name evokes the "royal road" of yakitori.
Michelin Guide-listed sushi counter: fish is selected at Tsuruhashi Market and the nigiri are formed small so you can sample as many items as possible.

Michelin Guide-listed Japanese restaurant; chef Tomonori Matsumura trained at a ryotei and in France, and his creed is to make ingredients taste even more like themselves — shrimp dishes use reduced shrimp stock.

Michelin Guide-listed yakitori built on premium Hinai-jidori chicken; the set menu blends techniques learned at Yakitori Ichimatsu with creative dishes like chicken shumai and confit, ending with takikomi-gohan or ramen.

Michelin Guide-listed yakitori where Hiroki Matsuoka ages Kagoshima free-range chicken and brushes skewers with a fragrant oil of his own, interspersed with soups and fried chicken dishes; meals end with earthenware-pot rice or chicken-broth ramen.

Michelin Guide-listed sushi counter of hinoki cypress: two kinds of sushi rice for harmony with toppings, soy-marinated tuna wrapped in nori tekkamaki-style — Edomae at heart with respect for Kansai culture.
One MICHELIN Star (2025 guide) Japanese counter where years of experience show in skilful work at counter and grill, convivial conversation and creative preparation.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2026) in Kitashinchi: creative kushiage that incorporates culinary influences from many countries — the sheer variety is endlessly fun.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2026) Chinese restaurant in Nishitemma.
Michelin Bib Gourmand: omakase-only Japanese cooking using fermented seasonings, no-nonsense dishes mixed with bar snacks that express the owner-chef's unaffected personality.
Michelin Guide-listed kushiage counter whose chef focuses on seafood in his kushikatsu prix fixe, frying tiger prawn rare to draw out its sweetness.
Michelin Guide-listed Kitashinchi kushiage that works extravagant ingredients such as foie gras, truffles and caviar into its skewers.

Michelin Bib Gourmand (2025 guide) shokudo in a detached Kitashinchi house hung with criss-crossing poles evoking Wakayama's Oto Fire Festival torches; expect gingered chicken liver, potato salad, deep-fried horse mackerel and seasonal dishes.
Michelin-selected (2026): an omakase set meal of tempura fried by the owner-chef, interspersed by the proprietress with dashi-simmered takiawase and hand-made oden.
One MICHELIN Star (2026) Naniwa kappo whose mission is cuisine matched to the guest; the menu, 'Yuno's omakase', strays freely from the norms of Japanese cuisine.
Michelin Guide-listed sushi shop turned from a delivery business into a counter by an Edomae-trained owner; sushi is served omakase, chosen to suit each guest's preferences.
Michelin-selected (2026) sushi restaurant in Ikutama, Tennoji-ku.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2025 guide) soba house with Oribe stoneware and earthen walls, serving two kinds of soba: fine-ground seiro and coarse-ground inaka.
Michelin-selected (2026) casual Italian eatery with traditional fare chalked on a blackboard — tripe stewed in tomato, marlin baked in herb-seasoned breadcrumbs, mushroom pappardelle.
One MICHELIN Star (2026) Japanese restaurant in a refined modern sukiya-style space: sashimi that showcases the chef's knife skills and grilled dishes over bincho charcoal.
Michelin Guide-listed sushi counter near Shitennoji temple.

Near-seventy-year-old okonomiyaki specialist by the Dōtonbori arcade, known for a cabbage-heavy, light batter; order the Ajinoya Mix (pork, squid, octopus, shrimp) or the negiyaki (Inside Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

places.n: Nishiya Shinsaibashi Honten (にし家 心斎橋本店)
places.w: Udon house in Higashi-Shinsaibashi that Mapple's editors credit as the origin of Osaka-style udon-chiri, the udon hot-pot eaten with a secret chiri vinegar; Rurubu also lists the honten. Open year-round.
places.nat: にし家 心斎橋本店

places.n: Marushō Gyōza-ten Honten (丸正餃子店 本店, Daitō)
places.w: Gyōza-only shop founded 1969 near JR Suminodō, reservation-only and famous for diners ordering four or five plates each; on Time Out Osaka's 'Higashi-Ōsaka 27 must-go restaurants' (Kita-Kawachi) and Rurubu's spot guide.
places.nat: 丸正餃子店 本店, Daitō

places.n: Saijō Gōshi Gaisha — Amanozake brewery (西條合資会社 天野酒, Kawachinagano)
places.w: Brewery founded 1718 that in 1971 recreated the monks' sake of nearby Amano-san Kongō-ji; production capped at ~70,000 bottles, winter brewery tours. Featured by OSAKA-INFO and Rurubu.
places.nat: 西條合資会社 天野酒, Kawachinagano

places.n: Kawachi Wine Kan (河内ワイン館, Habikino)
places.w: Family winery of ~90 years in the Habikino grape hills, Osaka's historic wine country; tours, tastings and make-your-own-label sessions. Covered by OSAKA-INFO (spot page and its Habikino winery-crawl feature) and Rurubu.
